minutes.headline: Commission continued two hearings for more site review, approved a septic and a planting project, and heard an earth removal permit.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard many hearings. The 390 Howard Street delineation was continued over erosion and unflagged wetlands, and the 2011 Fire Road 16 septic was continued for plan updates. The Trembley septic at 386 Sunset Lane, the Oakridge Road and Peninsula Drive notices of intent, and the Nashua River Watershed planting were approved. The captions end partway through the Northfield Road earth removal discussion.

public_comment.topic: Resident living downstream of 390 Howard Street reported silt from the brook has filled his pond, killing fish, for the third time in a year. He offered the commission access to his property and a neighbor's.
Abutter at Sunset Lane asked about wall elevations, grade, runoff and a large oak near the excavation at 386 Sunset Lane. He said he supports the revised plan.

decisions.decision: Bob will write to the building official on the commission's behalf about possible earth removal without a permit at 390 Howard Street.
Staff will inspect the erosion moving downhill toward Pearl Hill Brook and the downstream pond before the next hearing, with commissioners attending where possible.
Bob will work with the planning board consultant on a list of third-party wetland reviewers for 390 Howard Street.
The applicant at 2011 Fire Road 16 should locate trees of four to six inches and larger, show the true wetland edge and 50/100 foot buffers, and add silt fence with staked waddles.
Silt fence will be added to the straw waddles at 386 Sunset Lane.
The Nashua River Watershed Association may start planting now without waiting for the written letter, since the project is likely exempt.
The May 17 minutes will be taken up at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the 390 Howard Street wetland delineation to November 1 after hearing of erosion, missing flags and possible earth removal without a permit.
The Commission continued the 2011 Fire Road 16 septic filing to November 1; the applicant must show the true wetland edge, buffers and larger trees.
The Commission approved the 386 Sunset Lane replacement septic with an order of conditions adding silt fence to the straw waddle; Trembley recused.
The Commission approved the Nashua River Watershed planting with a negative determination, plus notices of intent for 38 Oakridge Road and 6 Peninsula Drive.
The Commission issued a positive determination on an amended order at 441 Townson Harbor Road; captions end before the Northfield Road earth removal review is resolved.

why_it_matters: A downstream resident reported silt filling his pond three times in a year, so the Howard Street outcome bears on brook and pond water quality that abutters and residents on the Pearl Hill Brook watershed depend on.
Septic replacements and work near wetlands go through this board, so conditions such as silt fencing and buffer mapping set what neighbors and the town can expect from projects near water.

The commission's letter to the building official on possible earth removal at 390 Howard Street, and the outcome of the 780 Northfield Road earth removal review.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The eight votes in our minutes all match the official minutes in item and outcome, and the differences are caption misspellings of names and addresses. The official minutes record three further votes that ours lacks: the Select Board letter on 780 Northfield Rd, the Robb Hill trails, and the 351 Mass. Ave. extension. They also record two dollar figures, $869,830.41 and $3,300, and several smaller decisions that ours omits.
